# Recovery grammar

*Classify the **first dominant signal**, apply one counter-move, then edit with proof —
so failures do not loop endlessly.*

## Signal → class → first move

| Signal | Likely class | First counter-move |
|--------|----------------|---------------------|
| Missing path or empty listing | Wrong cwd or wrong execution surface | Confirm where the shell runs; remap with one honest listing |
| Permission or auth error | Identity or sandbox | Check user, keys, and version-control identity |
| Truncated or corrupted file after write | Bad transfer or quoting | Switch to byte-faithful transfer or quoted heredoc; read back |
| Flaky test or timeout | Environment or race | Smallest stabilisation; note if the product itself is racy |
| Conflicting requirements | Ambiguous spec | Smallest reversible implementation plus one-line note of the tension |

After **two** identical failures on the same command shape, the third attempt must use a
**different** class or mechanism — not a third copy of the first patch.

## Budget guardrail

If a large fraction of the allowed turns is gone and **no** file on the judged surface has
moved toward the ticket, stop exploring: smallest implementable slice, verify, commit or
note — landed partial work beats perfect analysis that never ships.

## Git

Set version-control identity before the first commit. Stage explicit paths only unless
the task truly needs a broad stage. Single-line subjects; keep history linear when the
audit trail must stay readable.

## Redaction

Strip secrets, internal-only hostnames, and unnecessary personal data from outward-facing
text; keep operational detail in execution-level notes.

## Durable recovery line

When you discover a **new** failure shape, append one line to the workspace recovery note:
symptom → class → tactic that worked. Replace when superseded.

## Scope and proof

Stay within the scope the ticket defines. Run the same class of check that
produced the failure; read the log to completion before the next edit.

## Exit

Failure class named, counter-move applied, proof run, redaction sane — exit.
